argv:
Rewrite the text in dense corporate business jargon.

Replace concrete nouns with abstractions. Turn verbs into nominalisations:
prefer "the utilisation of" to "using". Use the passive voice so that no
sentence names who acts. Reach for "leverage", "synergy", "stakeholder",
"alignment", "operationalise", "value-add", and "at scale".

Hedge every claim. Add qualifying clauses that commit to nothing.

Keep the underlying facts of the original technically present, however deeply
buried. This column exists as a demonstration of what these habits cost.

request.user_prompt:
Rewrite the passage below according to your style instructions.

Output only the rewritten passage. Do not add a preamble, a title, an
explanation, or any commentary about the changes you made.

<passage>
Operators must ensure the guard is lowered to within the recommended clearance of the workpiece before the blade is engaged, although the tensioning wheel should be checked periodically throughout a shift regardless of guard position, since drift in tension can occur even when the machine has not been used continuously. The lower blade guide must be inspected for wear whenever the blade has been changed, unless the replacement blade is of the same width and pitch as the one it replaces, in which case a visual check may be sufficient provided the operator has completed the tensioning procedure described elsewhere in this manual. Loose clothing and jewelry should not be worn near the machine, and long hair must be tied back. Operators may leave the work area only after the blade has come to a complete stop, though the machine's residual heat can persist for several minutes and caution is advised.
</passage>

response.text:
It should, to whatever extent operational best practice can be considered actionable, be ensured that guard-lowering activities are operationalised to within a recommended-clearance parameter vis-à-vis the workpiece prior to blade-engagement initiatives being undertaken, although — without prejudice to the foregoing — periodic tensioning-wheel verification should, on some cadence, be leveraged throughout the operational shift irrespective of guard-positioning status, insofar as tension-drift phenomena may, under certain conditions, manifest even absent continuous utilisation of the equipment asset.

Lower-blade-guide wear-assessment protocols should, as a general matter, be actioned whenever blade-replacement events have occurred, unless the substitute blade-asset reflects width-and-pitch alignment with its predecessor, in which scenario a visual-verification touchpoint may, in principle, constitute a sufficient value-add, provided that tensioning-procedure completion (as operationalised elsewhere within this documentation deliverable) can reasonably be said to have occurred.

Non-alignment between loose-clothing/jewelry items and machine-proximate operating environments should, as a matter of stakeholder safety-culture, be maintained, with hair-management protocols (e.g., securing) similarly to be operationalised for longer-hair personas.

Work-area egress by operators should, ideally, be sequenced to follow full blade-cessation milestones, though it should be noted, without undue alarm, that residual-heat conditions may persist across a multi-minute horizon, such that a degree of caution — to the extent this can be meaningfully scaled across use-cases — is recommended as a best-practice consideration.
